title: Finite contact: complex models, regularity and isolated singularities
source_hypothesis: Scalar classical order-m PDO, nonzero homogeneous degree-1-m multiplier and homogeneous canonical reduction to xi1+i*x1^k*xin at the marked positive or negative last covector. Geometric fixed-contact hypotheses require a zero of exactly order k on every nearby real Hamilton curve. Regularity uses the favorable sign; isolated singularities use odd contact at the negative mark.
reviewed_arguments: The exact assumptions retain classical scalar symbols, the full geometric multiplier and canonical map, and a fixed contact order on every nearby real Hamilton curve. The marked sign and existence of each nearby zero are explicit.

The parameter Borel series realizes every prescribed transverse jet on one fixed normalized patch. The full Hamilton field has coefficient one in the distinguished derivative, so the residual jets are successively determined.

A numerator flat on the whole distinguished hypersurface divides smoothly by the complex model, including its characteristic intersection. Every differentiated pole is absorbed by an arbitrarily high flatness power; homogeneous degrees are retained.

The complete classical recursion fixes the left-right symbol differences at every order and retains all known residual terms. Ordinary summation, fixed supports and both elliptic inverses yield an actual smoothing intertwiner.

The solution graph operator is chosen of order zero and the source graph operator of order 1-m. This proves the exact regularity shift and preserves the prescribed threshold in the opposite-sign example. An explicit commuting model order reducer also recovers the original graph orders 1-m and zero and their elliptic composition.

The complex-valued line energy identity has the positive cross-term sign. The coercive bound follows from direct compactness using cell averages and polynomial tails, followed by the complete distributional integrating-factor argument.
Scaling retains all three norm powers. Reflection covers negative frequency only for even contact; the odd opposite sign has a nonzero Schwartz null mode and compact approximate null modes.

Partial Fourier transformation gives the full favorable conic estimate with all spectator variables. Compact mollification has an exact finite polynomial commutator, uniformly bounded in the ordinary order-zero class after every derivative.

Fatou gives the attained rough-input endpoint. Proper microlocal cutoffs, every smooth error and a finite nested-cone bootstrap yield the full Sobolev gain; one fixed final cutoff for all target orders proves microhypoellipticity.

Explicit compact concentrating packets have every-real Sobolev size lambda^r and source size O(lambda^(r+delta)). Their full Fourier tails justify microlocalization and prove sharpness of the uniform gain.

The opposite-sign integral is an actual tempered homogeneous solution. Every distributional differentiation is justified; integration by parts and the real damping show full smooth rapid tails away from the origin.
The complete Fourier transform has transverse scales lambda^delta and lambda^(1/2). All separated conic directions have rapid decay, including after spatial localization.

The actual weighted Fourier integral is comparable to the exact one-dimensional power integral for every real Sobolev order. The selected amplitude exponent gives membership exactly below the desired threshold, with logarithmic endpoint divergence.

Elliptic graph transfer gives one compactly localized distribution with smooth forcing on the original manifold, the exact positive ray through the marked covector and the same local Sobolev threshold.

The symplectic model companion constructs the projectors and inverse identities, proves their mapping properties and gives the microlocal solvability criterion. Global symplectic assembly treats proper patching and Hermitian normalization.
